extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors of observational epidemiology studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for reporting observational epidemiology studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), specifying which items should be included in a manuscript to ensure transparent, complete reporting. Includes links to explanation/elaboration papers and numerous STROBE extensions for specific topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE checklist items (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A checklist of items that should be included in articles reporting observational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The STROBE Statement aims to establish a checklist of items that should be included in articles reporting such research. STROBE checklist: combined; STROBE checklist: cohort studies; STROBE checklist: case-control studies; STROBE checklist: cross-sectional studies (Word/PDF available). The checklist is intended to provide guidance on how to report observational research well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report planned actions, actual conduct, findings, and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers need to know what was planned (and what was not), what was done, what was found, and what the results mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete and inadequate reporting hampers the assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of the studies reported in the medical literature. The checklist items are chosen to ensure transparency about planned versus done activities, clear presentation of results, and interpretation so readers can assess study validity and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: apply checklist to whole report
rubrics_metrics.description: The STROBE checklist applies to the whole report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asked 'Applies to the whole report or to individual sections of the report?' the STROBE entry indicates: Whole report. (Separate conference-abstract checklist exists for abstracts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Study-design-specific checklist selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the STROBE checklist version appropriate to your study design: cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendations were initially restricted to the three main analytical designs used in observational research: cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies. The website provides separate checklists for each design (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) as well as a combined checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE is for reporting, not for judging methodological quality or prescribing study conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendations are not prescriptions for designing or conducting studies, and the checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit guidance: 'Our recommendations are not prescriptions for designing or conducting studies. Also, the checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.' Use STROBE to improve reporting transparency rather than as a scoring tool of methodological quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to Explanation & Elaboration paper for detailed guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: An Explanation and Elaboration paper accompanies STROBE and gives detailed rationale and examples for the checklist items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation and elaboration paper (Vandenbroucke et al.) was published simultaneously in several journals; it provides expanded explanations and examples for each checklist item. Translations of the explanation and elaboration paper are also available (e.g., Japanese, Spanish).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use relevant STROBE extensions for specialised topics/designs
rubrics_metrics.description: For specific study types or topic areas, use the appropriate STROBE extension (e.g., STREGA, STROBE-ME, STROME-ID, STROBE-MR, STROBE-nut, RECORD, STROBE-EQUITY, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists many extensions and specialised reporting guidelines (STREGA for genetic association studies; STROBE-ME for molecular epidemiology; STROME-ID for molecular epidemiology of infectious diseases; STROBE-MR for Mendelian randomization; STROBE-nut for nutritional epidemiology; RECORD for routinely-collected health data; and many others). Use extensions when the study topic/design matches the extension's focus to get more specific reporting items.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE checklist for conference abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A draft STROBE checklist of items to be included when reporting observational studies in conference abstracts is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a first draft of the STROBE checklist for conference abstracts with a link to a full-text PDF. Use this abbreviated checklist when preparing abstracts for conferences to ensure key reporting elements are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage coordinated translations and extensions with the STROBE coordinating group
rubrics_metrics.description: If planning to produce translations, extensions, or to republish STROBE material, contact the STROBE coordinating group first to coordinate efforts and avoid duplication; the original authors hold the copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site requests that anyone intending to use the STROBE Statement for further extensions, translations or other STROBE-related work contact the coordinating group via the website first. Contact information is provided. This is a procedural requirement to ensure coordinated, copyright-respecting use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use online fillable checklists where available
rubrics_metrics.description: Online fillable STROBE checklists are available via GoodReports for case-control, cohort, and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes availability of online fillable checklists (GoodReports) which may facilitate completing the checklist during manuscript preparation.
